newsitem.title: USA: U.S. government to set up investor on-line - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: U.S. government to set up investor on-line - WSJ.

text.p: The U.S. government will launch this week a computer on-line service to help rich investors find small companies in which to invest, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

The newspaper said the Small Business Administration's Office of Advocacy and the Defense Department had created the service to help small companies get money to finance their operations in a less traditional way.
It said the service would be for companies that were still too small to go public or attract venture capital.

Potential investors would sign up to the service to get access to a list of company names and financial statements, it said, adding that about 300,000 companies qualified to be listed on the on-line service.
The newspaper said it was the first time that the government was trying to organize the informal world of "angel" financing.
An angel investor helps finance a small yet growing company.
